title: The loneliest firework display
caption: Barred spiral galaxy NGC 1559, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1559 · constellation Reticulum · about 50 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble view from the Wide Field Camera 3 shows NGC 1559, a barred spiral roughly 50 million light-years away in Reticulum, the Reticule, a southern constellation that astronomers rarely study. Its massive spiral arms are packed with star formation.

The galaxy holds the mass of around ten billion Suns, which sounds large but is almost 100 times less than the Milky Way. It is also receding from us at about 1300 km/s. On the sky it appears near the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of our nearest neighbors, but that is only a chance alignment. Physically, NGC 1559 is a genuine loner, with no nearby galaxies and no membership of any cluster.
For a loner, it has been busy. Astronomers have seen four supernovae, exploding stars, go off in NGC 1559, in 1984, 1986, 2005 and 2009.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.33 x 2.28 arcminutes) and distance (50 million light years), the frame spans roughly 34,000 × 33,000 light-years. Its light set out about 50 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using filters from the near-ultraviolet through visible light to the near-infrared. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: Some of the light recorded lies in the ultraviolet and near-infrared, beyond what the eye can see, and the exposures collect far more light than an eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The four explosions are cataloged as SN 1984J, SN 1986L, SN 2005df, which was a Type Ia, and SN 2009ib, a Type II-P supernova with an unusually long plateau in its fading light.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with massive spiral arms.
